name: 1315 Inglewood Drive

dates.note: The nomination states it twice, in two sections and two spellings of the style name: 'Ray Moulthrop's 1941 design for 1315 Inglewood Drive is very similar' and 'He designed the home at 1315 Inglewood Drive in the Garrison Colonial Revival style in 1941.'

refs.title: National Register of Historic Places, Inglewood Historic District Continuation Sheet, Cleveland Heights, Cuyahoga County, Ohio (2009 nomination)
refs.note: Section 7 reads 'Ray Moulthrop's 1941 design for 1315 Inglewood Drive is very similar' -- similar, that is, to 1251 Oakridge Road, described in the preceding sentences. Section 8's architect biography reads: 'Ray Moulthrop was a New York born architect. His office in 1927 was located at 500 Superior Avenue and at 241 Euclid Avenue in 1939. He was a regular contributor to residential architecture in Cleveland Heights. ... He designed the home at 1315 Inglewood Drive in the Garrison Colonial Revival style in 1941.'

refs.title: Inglewood Historic District, Cleveland Heights; NRHP reference No. 09000210, listed April 15, 2009 (as the Cuyahoga County listings table prints it)
refs.note: A DISTRICT listing shared with every contributing building in the neighbourhood, 1251 Oakridge Road included. It identifies a district, never this house.

note: Carried as the second half of a documented pair: one describer, two houses, twelve years apart, so what differs between them is the buildings and not the describer. The nomination's own comparison -- 'very similar' -- is the only statement of their relation and it is not elaborated; no dimension of either house is stated anywhere in the extract, so neither record carries a measurement.
